contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #206: Finite lattice representation and undecidability.
Audit of pkt:field-shifts under the actual retained-edge and shortcut hypotheses; classical ranks are at least nine and field degrees are arbitrary positive integers.

definitions.f_prime: intermediate usual group field exponent with reduced ratio u/v
definitions.a: source field exponent of a single admissible normalizer
definitions.s: upper natural scalar exponent of that same normalizer
definitions.scope: Manuscript statements are targets, not established external assumptions.

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 206 (Finite lattice representation and undecidability.; papers: Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability; A negative solution to the finite lattice representation problem; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/206.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Under pkt:field-shifts and its actual retained comparison and shortcut hypotheses, every admissible normalizer satisfies h divides s-a, and every packet of absolute constituent types has cardinality at most 2v.

For every actual retained edge of usual field exponents r,t, its nonempty union of absolute source digit supports on the target natural module lies in one residue class modulo gcd(r,t), including unitary twisted tensors and characteristic-two B/C realizations.

A single admissible shortcut normalizer induces compatible field exponents on both actual intermediate component realizations, including graph parts and characteristic-two B/C changes, so both edge congruences refer to the same intermediate exponent modulo h.

Conditionally on the support and compatible-normalizer hypotheses, support translation forces h divides s-a and the commuting field/diagram packet action has size at most 2v for every positive field degree.

The exact target is packets.tex lines 383-590; relevant Wiki-index retrieval found no entry, first bounded Jacobian discovery supplied no applicable representation-theoretic theorem, and neither finite arithmetic tests nor abstract digit countermodels settle this representation-theoretic target.
main:congruences: Some finite nonempty lattice is not the congruence lattice of any finite nonempty algebra of finite signature.
main:group: Some finite lattice is not a full subgroup interval [D,G] in any finite group.

The global universal finite congruence-lattice representation assertion is equivalent to the global universal finite-group subgroup-interval representation assertion; this is not pointwise equivalence for a fixed lattice.
The negative-solution manuscript's original-core factor transport and coordinate normal tests have the claimed subgroup-interval interpretations.
The negative-solution manuscript's classical subgroup catalogue and reductions cover all relevant long differing-label chains uniformly.
grw:remaining-paths: arbitrary-length reduced chains admit common-field classical endpoints and the five specified retained-path properties, including a single-digit nonlinear edge in each shortcut.

lift:edge-lifts: retained inner projections have nested characteristic quasisimple components with soluble quotients, compatible actual finite inclusions, and the asserted rational natural-module edge maps.
pkt:bounded-length: after fixed-spacing thinning, endpoint natural modules have absolute composition length at most 30B+62, uniformly in field degree.
pkt:semisimple, pkt:centralizer, pkt:multiplicity, and pkt:one-packet supply the claimed semisimple section, multiplicity bound 15, and one-large-packet alternative.
cls:chain-rigidity: the manuscript's tested differing-label chains have an absolute length bound, through natural-endpoint irreducibility and irreducible-restriction rigidity.
The negative-solution manuscript's decorated Boolean rank-four lattice enforces all required forward and reverse chain tests while preserving the asserted joins, meets, and full intervals.
glue:contradiction: in a minimal subgroup-interval representation, the socle/action correspondence and proper-face extension compatibility force the forbidden full-union common extension.

m:main: the colored-graph characterization, undecidability of finite congruence representation, a finite description of the least counterexample with size greater than seven, and undecidability of finite subgroup-interval recognition all hold.
f:criterion: the stated finite colored complete graph criterion is equivalent to full finite congruence-lattice representability, rather than only an embedding.

f:negative-family and f:thm-almost-simple-reduction: the private affine-chart normal tests and extension-kernel exclusions yield the claimed full starting-interval obstruction and almost-simple reduction.
r:reverse-exclusion, c:classical-conclusion, and c:alternating-conclusion hold uniformly for the protected ancestor paths.
t:weighted-realization: every relevant finite realization admits the common cell alignment and simultaneous numerical readings encoding both addition and multiplication.
n:template-bound: a computable template bound controls affirmative witness size independently of unknown encoded weights.
n:undecidable: a finite-representability decider would decide Diophantine solvability by the claimed total effective reduction.
n:interval-undecidable: recognizing full finite-group subgroup intervals is undecidable, using an ambient-group-order bound rather than only an algebra-carrier-size bound.

q:minimum: explicit order-table formulas and a Busy Beaver bound finitely specify a minimum-cardinality nonrepresentable lattice, all smaller lattices are representable, and its size is greater than seven.

For all integer periods and nonempty supports in a single divisor-residue class, translation invariance modulo the period forces the shift to be divisible by that divisor; modular arithmetic progressions have the stated support and no-carry properties, including odd unitary doubling; for any finite group, commuting g,d with d^2=1 and either g^v=1 or g^v=d generate a subgroup of cardinality at most 2v when v>0.

import Mathlib

namespace FieldShift

theorem shift_divisible_of_residue_support
    (E : Set ℤ) (h r c k : ℤ)
    (hne : E.Nonempty)
    (hperiod : h ∣ r)
    (hresidue : ∀ x ∈ E, h ∣ x - c)
    (htranslate : ∀ x ∈ E, ∃ y ∈ E, r ∣ x + k - y) :
    h ∣ k := by
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hne
  obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := htranslate x hx
  have hwrap : h ∣ x + k - y := dvd_trans hperiod hxy
  have hsum : h ∣ (x + k - y) + (y - c) - (x - c) :=
    dvd_sub (dvd_add hwrap (hresidue y hy)) (hresidue x hx)
  have heq : (x + k - y) + (y - c) - (x - c) = k := by ring
  rwa [heq] at hsum

theorem progression_residue
    (h t r t0 j q : ℤ) (ht : h ∣ t) (hr : h ∣ r) :
    h ∣ (t0 + j * t - q * r) - t0 := by
  have hmultiple : h ∣ j * t - q * r :=
    dvd_sub (dvd_mul_of_dvd_right ht j) (dvd_mul_of_dvd_right hr q)
  have heq : (t0 + j * t - q * r) - t0 = j * t - q * r := by ring
  rwa [heq]

theorem progression_no_wrap
    (b t j : ℤ) (ht : 0 < t) (hj0 : 0 ≤ j) (hjb : j < b) :
    0 ≤ j * t ∧ j * t < b * t := by
  exact ⟨mul_nonneg hj0 ht.le, mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hjb ht⟩

theorem progression_mod_representative
    (b t j : ℤ) (ht : 0 < t) (hj0 : 0 ≤ j) (hjb : j < b) :
    (j * t) % (b * t) = j * t := by
  exact Int.emod_eq_of_lt (progression_no_wrap b t j ht hj0 hjb).1
    (progression_no_wrap b t j ht hj0 hjb).2

theorem progression_distinct_mod
    (b t i j : ℤ) (ht : t ≠ 0)
    (hi : i ∈ Set.Ico 0 b) (hj : j ∈ Set.Ico 0 b) :
    Int.ModEq (b * t) (i * t) (j * t) ↔ i = j := by
  constructor
  · intro hmod
    have hindices := Int.ModEq.mul_right_cancel' ht hmod
    change i % b = j % b at hindices
    simpa only [Int.emod_eq_of_lt hi.1 hi.2, Int.emod_eq_of_lt hj.1 hj.2] using hindices
  · rintro rfl
    exact Int.ModEq.rfl

theorem odd_doubling_modEq_iff
    (b : ℕ) (hb : Odd b) (i j : ℕ) :
    Nat.ModEq b (2 * i) (2 * j) ↔ Nat.ModEq b i j := by
  constructor
  · intro hmod
    exact hmod.cancel_left_of_coprime hb.coprime_two_right
  · intro hmod
    exact hmod.mul_left 2

theorem odd_doubling_distinct_mod
    (b : ℕ) (hb : Odd b) (i j : ℕ) (hi : i < b) (hj : j < b) :
    Nat.ModEq b (2 * i) (2 * j) ↔ i = j := by
  rw [odd_doubling_modEq_iff b hb i j]
  exact ⟨fun hmod => hmod.eq_of_lt_of_lt hi hj, fun h => h ▸ Nat.ModEq.rfl⟩

theorem synchronized_differences_add
    (h a a1 s : ℤ) (hfirst : h ∣ a1 - a) (hsecond : h ∣ s - a1) :
    h ∣ s - a := by
  have hsum : h ∣ (a1 - a) + (s - a1) := dvd_add hfirst hsecond
  have heq : (a1 - a) + (s - a1) = s - a := by ring
  rwa [heq] at hsum

theorem commuting_pair_integer_normal_form
    {G : Type*} [Group G] (g d : G) (hcommute : Commute g d)
    {x : G} (hx : x ∈ Subgroup.closure ({g, d} : Set G)) :
    ∃ m n : ℤ, g ^ m * d ^ n = x := by
  induction hx using Subgroup.closure_induction with
  | mem x hx =>
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl
    · exact ⟨1, 0, by simp⟩
    · exact ⟨0, 1, by simp⟩
  | one => exact ⟨0, 0, by simp⟩
  | mul x y hx hy ihx ihy =>
    obtain ⟨m, n, rfl⟩ := ihx
    obtain ⟨p, q, rfl⟩ := ihy
    refine ⟨m + p, n + q, ?_⟩
    rw [zpow_add, zpow_add]
    exact (hcommute.zpow_zpow p n).mul_mul_mul_comm (g ^ m) (d ^ q)
  | inv x hx ih =>
    obtain ⟨m, n, rfl⟩ := ih
    refine ⟨-m, -n, ?_⟩
    simpa only [zpow_neg, mul_inv_rev] using (hcommute.zpow_zpow m n).inv_inv.eq

theorem commuting_pair_card_le
    {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (g d : G) (hcommute : Commute g d) :
    Nat.card (Subgroup.closure ({g, d} : Set G)) ≤ orderOf g * orderOf d := by
  let H := Subgroup.closure ({g, d} : Set G)
  have hg : g ∈ H := Subgroup.subset_closure (by simp)
  have hd : d ∈ H := Subgroup.subset_closure (by simp)
  have hgz : Subgroup.zpowers g ≤ H := by
    rw [Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure]
    exact (Subgroup.closure_le H).mpr (Set.singleton_subset_iff.mpr hg)
  have hdz : Subgroup.zpowers d ≤ H := by
    rw [Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure]
    exact (Subgroup.closure_le H).mpr (Set.singleton_subset_iff.mpr hd)
  let f : Subgroup.zpowers g × Subgroup.zpowers d → H :=
    fun p => ⟨p.1.1 * p.2.1, H.mul_mem (hgz p.1.2) (hdz p.2.2)⟩
  have hsurjective : Function.Surjective f := by
    intro x
    obtain ⟨m, n, heq⟩ := commuting_pair_integer_normal_form g d hcommute x.property
    refine ⟨(⟨g ^ m, Subgroup.zpow_mem_zpowers g m⟩,
      ⟨d ^ n, Subgroup.zpow_mem_zpowers d n⟩), ?_⟩
    exact Subtype.ext heq
  calc
    Nat.card H ≤ Nat.card (Subgroup.zpowers g × Subgroup.zpowers d) :=
      Nat.card_le_card_of_surjective f hsurjective
    _ = orderOf g * orderOf d := by
      rw [Nat.card_prod, Nat.card_zpowers, Nat.card_zpowers]

theorem closure_pair_eq_zpowers_of_power
    {G : Type*} [Group G] (g d : G) (v : ℕ) (hpower : g ^ v = d) :
    Subgroup.closure ({g, d} : Set G) = Subgroup.zpowers g := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · refine (Subgroup.closure_le _).mpr ?_
    intro x hx
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
    rcases hx with hx | hx
    · rw [hx]
      exact Subgroup.mem_zpowers g
    · rw [hx, ← hpower]
      exact Subgroup.npow_mem_zpowers g v
  · rw [Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure]
    apply Subgroup.closure_mono
    exact Set.singleton_subset_iff.mpr (by simp)

theorem field_diagram_group_card_bound
    {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (g d : G) (v : ℕ)
    (hcommute : Commute g d) (hd : d ^ 2 = 1) (hv : 0 < v)
    (hpower : g ^ v = 1 ∨ g ^ v = d) :
    Nat.card (Subgroup.closure ({g, d} : Set G)) ≤ 2 * v := by
  rcases hpower with hpower | hpower
  · calc
      Nat.card (Subgroup.closure ({g, d} : Set G)) ≤ orderOf g * orderOf d :=
        commuting_pair_card_le g d hcommute
      _ ≤ v * 2 :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul (orderOf_le_of_pow_eq_one hv hpower)
          (orderOf_le_of_pow_eq_one (by decide : 0 < 2) hd)
      _ = 2 * v := Nat.mul_comm v 2
  · have hdouble : g ^ (2 * v) = 1 := by
      calc
        g ^ (2 * v) = (g ^ v) ^ 2 := by rw [← pow_mul, Nat.mul_comm]
        _ = 1 := by rw [hpower, hd]
    rw [closure_pair_eq_zpowers_of_power g d v hpower]
    rw [Nat.card_zpowers]
    exact orderOf_le_of_pow_eq_one (by omega : 0 < 2 * v) hdouble

end FieldShift

This is a true auxiliary observation, not a counterexample to a manuscript assertion.

Their pullback weight maps send omega_i(C) to omega_i(B) for i<ell and omega_ell(C) to 2*omega_ell(B), and send omega_i(B) to 2*omega_i(C) for i<ell and omega_ell(B) to omega_ell(C).
external_assumptions.source: Dowd and Sin, On representations of algebraic groups in characteristic two, Communications in Algebra 24 (1996), 2597-2686; cited author version obtained and read.
external_assumptions.locator: Author version I.3.1, equations (1)-(2), and I.3.2, equations (1)-(2)

external_assumptions.statement: For a simply connected algebraic group in characteristic p, irreducible rational modules have the unique restricted Frobenius tensor decomposition. For the finite universal classical fixed-point group of tau*F_p^r in the ranks under audit, the p^r-restricted highest weights restrict irreducibly and distinctly and exhaust the absolute simple modules.
external_assumptions.source: Steinberg, Lectures on Chevalley Groups, original Yale 1967 notes with 1968 acknowledgement; original scan obtained and read.

external_assumptions.statement: For a quasi-compact morphism of schemes locally of finite presentation, the image of every locally constructible subset is locally constructible. In particular a finite-type orbit map between affine varieties has constructible image.
external_assumptions.source: The Stacks Project, Tag 054K, Theorem 29.23.3 as obtained and read on 2026-11-05; includes the quasi-compact and locally finite-presentation hypotheses.

claims.natural_statement: Under pkt:field-shifts and its actual retained comparison and shortcut hypotheses, every admissible normalizer satisfies h divides s-a, and every packet of absolute constituent types has cardinality at most 2v.

external_assumptions.statement: Automorphisms of the finite universal classical groups in the ranks under audit are products of inner, diagonal, diagram and field automorphisms; for twisted groups the diagram involution is already a field power. In the high-rank classical cases natural realizations implement these by semilinear similarities or, for type A graph operations, correlations.
external_assumptions.source: Steinberg, Lectures on Chevalley Groups, original Yale 1967 notes with 1968 acknowledgement; original scan obtained and read. Natural-matrix implementations are proved directly in the audit report.

claims.natural_statement: irr:natural-endpoints: in the remaining configurations of grw:remaining-paths, arbitrarily long chains have arbitrarily long subchains on which every natural endpoint module restricts absolutely irreducibly to each earlier endpoint. This manuscript assertion remains unverified.

routes.retired_because: The initial scope map bundled natural-endpoint irreducibility into chain rigidity; the refined decomposition records irr:natural-endpoints as its own open obligation. This is a dependency refinement, not a mathematical counterexample.

The explicit pullback omega_1+omega_ell -> omega_1+2*omega_ell changes ordinary supports from {0} to {0,1}; compatibility must instead be proved using the intrinsic field exponent, not invariance of all digits. This stronger invariance was never asserted by the manuscript.
